statement: The function returns a result r and, for that r, r = true if and only if there exists a finite sequence of indices p_0, ..., p_k with k >= 0 such that p_0 = start, for every t with 0 <= t <= k we have 0 <= p_t < n, for every t with 0 <= t < k we have p_{t+1} = p_t + arr[p_t] or p_{t+1} = p_t - arr[p_t], and arr[p_k] = 0. Equivalently, start can reach a zero-valued index by zero or more legal jumps.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies the problem constraints: n >= 1; n <= 50000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] < n; and 0 <= start < n.

statement: The function returns a result r on (arr, start) and a result r2 on (arr2, start), and r = r2.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies the problem constraints: n >= 1; n <= 50000; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] < n; and 0 <= start < n. Let R be the set of indices reachable from start under arr by legal jump paths. Let arr2 be any slice of length n such that 0 <= arr2[i] < n for every i with 0 <= i < n, and arr2[i] = arr[i] for every i in R.
